exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal vs. caesarean section)
Timing of gluten introduction in childhood
cohort: The study participants consisted of 1,226 Slovak respondents, including 534 patients with celiac disease and 692 controls.
finding: Being female, having a positive family history of CD, suffering from another autoimmune disease, and frequent use of antibiotics during childhood were associated with increased odds of CD, while breastfeeding in infancy showed a protective effect.
mod_finding: The mode of delivery (vaginal vs. caesarean section) did not show a statistically significant effect on the odds of developing CD.
